messages:
morgan: did a perfetto end-to-end capture for client->gateway->runtime yesterday. seeing a high tail on some requests when kv cache sparsity is high — attaching trace: https://perfetto.app/trace/abc123 (large capture)

morgan: quick summary: batch size 256, avg latency ~48ms, 95p ~72ms, but a subset of requests hit 200-320ms. spikes correlate with a repeated kernel handoff pattern and extra KV fetch kernels. :thinking:

julia: can you paste the hotspot timeline? is it during token gen or prefill? :eyes:

morgan: prefill mostly. timeline shows client->gateway span is flat ~6ms, gateway->runtime handshake ~4ms, but runtime shows repeated small kernels: `kv_fetch_batch`, `kv_prefetch_worker`, `cuda_matmul_v2`, `softmax_fused`. pattern is: matmul -> softmax -> kv_fetch -> matmul (kernel flip) which stalls the pipeline.

morgan: small log excerpt from the runtime around one of the long reqs:
```
[2026-03-15T23:12:10.342Z] req=0x1f2 stage=prefill kv_hit_ratio=0.11 kv_fetch_ms=18.3 kernel_seq=softmax_fused->kv_fetch_batch->cuda_matmul_v2
[2026-03-15T23:12:10.360Z] req=0x1f2 stage=gen kv_batch_id=42 latency_ms=212
```

sai: hmmm low kv_hit_ratio is suspect. are we falling back to a different kernel because kv cache misses change the sequence length distribution (or the presence of KV fetch DMA transfers)?

morgan: exact theory. perfetto shows bursts of NVTX spans labeled `kv_dma_submit` that precede the extra kernels. nsys summary on the longest sample:
```
GPU activities: kernels 86%, memcpy 9%, stalls 5%
Top kernels: kv_fetch_batch (28% time), cuda_matmul_v2 (24%), softmax_fused (12%)
```

ben: that ordering is bad — the runtime is doing kernel selection per micro-step and not optimizing for upcoming KV fetches. if kv_fetch is coming, we should prefer the kernel that tolerates memory IO overlap or prefetch the KV earlier.

julia: do we have batching heuristic logs? iirc we switch batch strategy if observed prefix variance > 0.2 which can cause batch splitting. could that interact?

morgan: yes. heuristic trace shows `batch_strategy=adaptive_split` kicking in when kv sparseness >0.15, which reduces effective concurrency and causes more small batches where kv miss cost isn't amortized.

perf-bot: Attached perfetto timeline marker: <https://perfetto.app/trace/abc123> — tag `kv-sparsity-030`

sai: next steps I suggest:
- reproduce with deterministic kv sparsity generator (I can spin up a client to hit keys with controlled reuse)
- run perfetto + nsys on runtime-only to get kernel timestamps with thread id
- try enabling kv-prefetch heuristic in runtime (`KV_PREFETCH=1`) to see if it overlaps memcpy and reduces kernel flip

morgan: I've already got a replay tool to simulate sparsity. command to reproduce locally: `infra/prof/run_perfetto --scenario kv-sparsity --reuse 0.12 --batch 256 --out /tmp/trace.pb`

ben: also try forcing kernel selection policy `KERSEL=stable` that prefers fused kernels even if hit ratio low — may reduce handoff penalty. add config: `runtime.config.kernel_selector=stable_prefer_fused`

julia: if prefetch + stable kernel reduce tail, we should add a micro-benchmark and regression test in CI (small perfetto golden trace) so we don't regress back.

morgan: agreed. I'll run the reproducer and attach a trimmed perfetto. planning to test three variants: baseline, KV_PREFETCH=1, KERSEL=stable_prefer_fused. will post results in this thread.

morgan: preliminary results (short run): baseline 95p=78ms, KV_PREFETCH 95p=66ms, KERSEL stable 95p=63ms, combined 95p=55ms. tails reduced but still occasional outliers ~120ms.

sai: promising. for the remaining outliers, capture nsys timeline with per-kernel timestamps (use `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt` and `--sample=long`) and paste kernel timestamps — we want to see if memcpy happens on the critical path or is serialized.

morgan: will do. one more thought: the kernel selection table has sequence-length thresholds that are computed from past 10s window. with sparse KV misses, the window is noisy. we may need a smoothing factor or to include KV hit ratio as a feature in the kernel selector.

ben: yup. adding KV-hit as an input to kernel selection could let us pick kernels that preemptively overlap DMA. Might be a quick win.

morgan: thanks all. I'll run nsys traces for 20 samples and upload trimmed traces + a small perf regression PR with the KV_PREFETCH toggle exposed. tagging @julia for CI regression test help. :thumbsup:
